title: Explain why to use slicer in docs/why-slicer.md
lead: Neither the README nor `docs/` says why someone would use slicer. The README intro says what slicer is: roadmap and slice management, AI-friendly, JSON state in git, stdlib only. Nothing pairs the workflow problems people hit with the features that fix them. This slice adds `docs/why-slicer.md`, a one-screen page that does that, and links it from the README.
findings_note: owner, 2026-10-14: README and docs never say why to use slicer; asked for a brief problem-to-feature page under docs, linked from the README

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: The owner asked for this on 2026-10-14: something brief that highlights the features and the workflow problems slicer smooths out. A reader deciding whether to adopt slicer currently has to piece that together from the command reference. One short page lets them judge quickly, and the README links send them there.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `docs/why-slicer.md` (new).
- `README.md`: a one-line pointer at the end of the intro (after the "Stdlib Python 3.11+, no dependencies." line), plus a first entry in `## Documentation`.
- `tests/test_docs_coverage.py`: the link tests below.
- `CHANGELOG.md` `[Unreleased]`.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
- `test_Readme_LinksWhySlicer_InIntroAndDocumentationList`: `README.md` links `docs/why-slicer.md` once before `## Install` and once under `## Documentation`.
- `test_WhySlicer_RelativeLinks_Resolve`: every relative Markdown link in `docs/why-slicer.md` points to a file that exists in the repo. A `#anchor` part is ignored, and `http(s)` links are skipped.

sections.heading: Implement
Check
sections.body:
- The full suite passes on Python 3.11+.
- Each claim on the page is checked against the code or the linked doc. The report lists each bullet with the file and line that supports it.
- `slicer check` and `git diff --check` pass.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: Worktree `.worktrees/s269`, branch `feature/s269-why-slicer`. Commit only on the branch. Merging and pushing wait for the owner.

sections.heading: Boundary
sections.body:
- Docs only. No change under `src/`, and no change to command behaviour or output.
- Every claim on the page must be true of the current code and docs. Name only features that exist, and link each to the doc that covers it. No roadmap promises and no comparisons with named products.
- The README intro and the Documentation list each gain one link. Nothing else in the README changes.
